1995.title: Larsen A Ice Shelf Collapse
1995.description: The Larsen A ice shelf on the Antarctic Peninsula fractured completely after decades of global warming, releasing thousands of icebergs into the ocean. Impact: Approximately 1,600 km² of ice was lost, signaling severe instability in the Antarctic ice system. Casualties: No human fatalities; disrupted local marine ecosystems
1995.source: National Snow and Ice Data Center

1995.title: Chicago Record Heatwave
1995.description: An extreme heatwave struck the Midwestern United States, with heat indices reaching 48°C for several consecutive days due to the urban heat island effect. Impact: Overloaded power grids, killed urban vegetation, and transformed climate crisis response protocols in the US. Casualties: 739 deaths
1995.source: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC)

1995.title: Omai Gold Mine Cyanide Spill
1995.description: The tailings dam at the Omai gold mine failed, leaking over 4 billion liters of cyanide-laced liquid into the Essequibo River. Impact: Guyana's largest river basin was heavily contaminated, destroying fisheries and river ecosystems for years. Casualties: No direct human deaths; millions of aquatic organisms killed

1995.title: COP1 Climate Summit in Berlin
1995.description: The first Conference of the Parties to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC) was held to manage global emissions. Impact: Adopted the 'Berlin Mandate,' establishing the first international legal foundation for greenhouse gas reductions. Casualties: None

1995.title: Great Floods of the Rhine and Meuse
1995.description: Continuous heavy rain combined with rapid snowmelt caused record water levels in the Rhine and Meuse rivers, leading to severe flooding in Central Europe. Impact: Submerged vast agricultural areas, forcing over 250.000 people in the Netherlands to evacuate due to dike failure risks. Casualties: Approximately 40 deaths across Europe; billions of USD in damages

1995.title: Super Typhoon Angela (Rosing) Devastates SE Asia
1995.description: One of the strongest storms of the 1990s, with wind gusts of 290 km/h, made a direct hit on Luzon Island. Impact: Caused widespread landslides, destroyed over 96.000 homes, and ravaged coastal nature reserves. Casualties: 936 deaths; economic damage over 418 million USD

1995.title: Soufrière Hills Volcano Awakens
1995.description: The Soufrière Hills volcano erupted violently after a long dormant period, burying the capital Plymouth under thick ash. Impact: Turned more than two-thirds of the island into an uninhabitable exclusion zone and destroyed endemic vegetation. Casualties: No deaths in the initial phase due to evacuation; forced the migration of the majority of the population

1995.title: Historic Floods Cause Crop Failure in North Korea
1995.description: Unprecedented heavy flooding destroyed most of the nation's key agricultural lands. Impact: Destroyed 330,000 hectares of farmland and lost 1.9 million tons of food, triggering a historic famine. Casualties: Hundreds of direct deaths from flooding; tens of thousands indirectly affected
1995.source: United Nations Department of Humanitarian Affairs

1995.title: Record Drought in the United Kingdom
1995.description: The summer of 1995 was recorded as the driest in England since 1766, accompanied by a prolonged heatwave. Impact: Reservoir levels dropped to alarmingly low levels, causing widespread wildfires on moorlands. Casualties: Estimated increase in mortality among the elderly due to heatstroke

1995.title: Great Hanshin Earthquake and Urban Pollution
1995.description: A 6.9 magnitude earthquake devastated the city of Kobe, releasing large amounts of toxic gases from ruptured pipelines. Impact: Caused massive fires, leaked industrial chemicals into Kobe Bay, and severely damaged coastal infrastructure. Casualties: 6,434 deaths; over 43,000 injured

1995.title: Hurricane Opal Ravages Coastal Ecosystems
1995.description: A Category 4 hurricane swept through the Gulf of Mexico and made landfall in Florida, bringing massive storm surges that eroded dunes. Impact: Caused the most severe coastal erosion in decades in Florida, destroying sea turtle habitats. Casualties: 59 deaths; 4.7 billion USD in damages

1995.title: Mount Ruapehu Ash Eruptions
1995.description: New Zealand's largest volcano became active again, sending ash plumes up to 10 km into the atmosphere. Impact: Contaminated surrounding lakes with acid, destroyed mountain vegetation, and paralyzed the aviation industry. Casualties: No human fatalities due to effective safety perimeters

1995.title: Ecological Crisis and the Brent Spar Rig Dispute
1995.description: Shell's plan to sink the Brent Spar oil storage buoy into the deep Atlantic met with fierce protests and blockades by environmental groups. Impact: Forced energy corporations to change marine industrial waste disposal processes, leading to a European ban on dumping solid waste at sea. Casualties: No human fatalities; severe damage to corporate reputation

1995.title: Hurricane Roxanne Devastates Mexican Coral Reefs
1995.description: A Category 3 hurricane moved erratically and maintained intensity for an unusually long time in the Gulf of Mexico, creating destructive waves. Impact: Destroyed the structure of the Cozumel coral reefs and severely eroded mangrove forests along the Yucatán Peninsula. Casualties: 29 deaths; over 1.5 billion USD in material damages

1995.title: Historic Flash Floods in the Mississippi River Valley
1995.description: Severe thunderstorms triggered violent flash floods along the lower Mississippi River and in Louisiana. Impact: Rainfall exceeding 500mm in a short period flooded riverside nature reserves and washed away nutrient-rich topsoil. Casualties: 33 deaths; property damage exceeded 3 billion USD

2000.title: Baia Mare Cyanide Spill Disaster
2000.description: A tailings dam at the Aurul gold mine burst, releasing 100,000 m³ of water with high cyanide concentrations into the environment. Impact: Contaminated the clean water supply of 2.5 million people, killing all aquatic life in the Somes, Tisa, and Danube rivers. Casualties: Hundreds of tons of dead fish; considered the worst ecological disaster in Europe since Chernobyl.

2000.title: Great Mozambique Flood
2000.description: Intense heavy rains caused by the consecutive effects of Cyclones Leon-Eline and Gloria led to the worst flooding in 50 years in the Limpopo River basin. Impact: Submerged 1,400 km² of agricultural land, destroyed livelihoods, and triggered an environmental health crisis. Casualties: Approximately 800 deaths; tens of thousands of livestock washed away

2000.title: Cerro Grande Wildfire
2000.description: A controlled burn by park rangers went out of control due to high winds, becoming a catastrophic wildfire in New Mexico. Impact: Burned over 19,000 hectares of wild forest, destroyed over 400 homes, and directly threatened Los Alamos National Laboratory. Casualties: No human fatalities; over 25.000 people evacuated

2000.title: Martin County Coal Slurry Spill
2000.description: A coal waste impoundment failed, releasing over 1.1 million m³ of toxic coal slurry into underground caves and streams. Impact: Heavily contaminated the clean water source for tens of thousands of residents and killed all aquatic life along 120 km of Kentucky's river systems. Casualties: Considered an inland ecological disaster worse than the Exxon Valdez oil spill

2000.title: Westchester Barge Oil Spill on the Mississippi
2000.description: The barge Westchester collided heavily, leaking over 2.1 million liters of crude oil into the lower Mississippi River. Impact: Created an oil slick stretching tens of kilometers, directly threatening wild bird sanctuaries in coastal wetlands. Casualties: No human casualties; severely contaminated habitats for wildlife

2000.title: Cerro Grande Fire Threatens US Nuclear Center
2000.description: A prescribed fire by the National Park Service (NPS) escaped control due to high winds, creating a massive wildfire that reached Los Alamos, New Mexico. Impact: Burned over 19,000 hectares, severely threatened nuclear waste storage areas at Los Alamos National Laboratory, forcing an emergency evacuation. Casualties: No direct fatalities, but over 400 homes destroyed; approximately 1 billion USD in damages

2000.title: Adoption of the Cartagena Protocol on Biosafety
2000.description: The first international treaty governing the cross-border movement of living modified organisms (LMOs) was adopted. Impact: Established a legal framework to protect global biodiversity from potential risks posed by modern biotechnology. Casualties: None

2000.title: Miyake-jima Eruption and Toxic Gas Leak
2000.description: Mount Oyama erupted continuously, releasing massive amounts of highly toxic sulfur dioxide (SO₂). Impact: Concentrated toxic gases devastated all natural vegetation, forcing all island residents to evacuate for several years. Casualties: Forced all 3.600 residents to evacuate urgently by ship

2000.title: Catastrophic Flooding in the Ganges Basin and West Bengal
2000.description: Extreme monsoon rains caused dike systems to overflow in West Bengal and neighboring Bangladesh. Impact: Submerged millions of hectares of rice, eroded riverine ecological corridors, and caused widespread groundwater pollution. Casualties: Over 1,200 deaths; approximately 20 million people directly affected

2000.title: Walkerton Groundwater Contamination
2000.description: Heavy rains washed livestock manure from agricultural farms into the town's municipal drinking water wells. Impact: Drinking water contaminated with a virulent strain of E. coli, exposing massive gaps in agricultural groundwater safety management. Casualties: 7 deaths; over 2,300 people severely ill

2000.title: Sinking of the Chemical Tanker Ievoli Sun in the English Channel
2000.description: The Italian-flagged tanker carrying oil and chemicals sank off the English Channel during a storm with 6,000 tons of toxic chemicals (including styrene and MEK). Impact: Chemical leaks poisoned coastal marine ecosystems in France and the Channel Islands, forcing a long-term large-scale fishing ban. Casualties: 14 sailors rescued; localized poisoning of seabed ecosystems

2000.title: Collapse of the COP6 Climate Summit in The Hague
2000.description: International negotiations on how to implement emission reductions under the Kyoto Protocol collapsed due to major disagreements. Impact: Delayed global legal actions against global warming trends for several years. Casualties: None

2000.title: Launch of the Millennium Ecosystem Assessment (MA)
2000.description: UN Secretary-General Kofi Annan officially launched a major international program to assess the health of Earth's biosphere. Impact: Mobilized over 1,300 scientists worldwide to establish a comprehensive scientific database on ecosystem services. Casualties: None

2000.title: Hurricane Keith Devastates Central American Ecosystems
2000.description: A slow-moving Category 4 hurricane made landfall in Belize and Mexico. Impact: Colossal rainfall caused severe flooding and destroyed coastal reefs due to the massive influx of freshwater from inland. Casualties: 68 deaths; heavy material damages

2000.title: Autumn Floods in Western Europe
2000.description: Consecutive low-pressure systems caused unprecedented heavy rainfall in the UK, Switzerland, and Northern Italy. Impact: Caused severe landslides in the Alps and flooded downstream agricultural valleys. Casualties: Over 40 deaths; tens of thousands displaced across Europe

2005.title: Hurricane Katrina Devastates the Gulf Coast
2005.description: A Category 5 superstorm completely breached the levee system, submerging 80% of New Orleans. Impact: Record damage of 125 billion USD; caused an urban ecological pollution disaster due to chemical, crude oil, and bacteria-laden sewage leaks. Casualties: Over 1,800 deaths

2005.title: Kyoto Protocol Officially Enters into Force
2005.description: The first legally binding international treaty requiring industrialized nations to reduce greenhouse gas emissions officially became active. Impact: Created a mandatory framework for 37 developed countries to mitigate the negative impacts of climate change. Casualties: None

2005.title: Songhua River Chemical Pollution Incident
2005.description: A series of explosions at a Jilin chemical plant released about 100 tons of toxic benzene into the Songhua River. Impact: Created a toxic chemical slick over 80 km long, paralyzing the river basin's ecosystem and forcing a water shutdown for millions. Casualties: 6 deaths at the plant; severe destruction of aquatic populations

2005.title: Catastrophic Flooding in Mumbai
2005.description: The financial hub of Mumbai recorded a record 944mm of rain in just 24 hours due to extreme monsoon activity. Impact: Completely paralyzed the urban drainage system, causing massive clean water pollution due to overflowing sewage. Casualties: Over 1,000 deaths; economic damage over 1.2 billion USD

2005.title: Devastating Earthquake in Kashmir
2005.description: A 7.6 magnitude earthquake hit the rugged mountain region of Kashmir, triggering thousands of landslides. Impact: Flattened entire mountain towns, severely destroying geological structures and protective forests. Casualties: Over 86,000 deaths; millions left homeless before winter

2005.title: Hurricane Wilma Sets Record Atmospheric Pressure
2005.description: The strongest storm in Atlantic history ever recorded, with central pressure dropping to a record 882 hPa. Impact: Catastrophically ravaged coastal ecosystems of the Yucatán Peninsula and Florida, destroying shallow coral reefs. Casualties: 87 deaths; material damages exceeding 22 billion USD

2005.title: Hurricane Rita Devastates Gulf of Mexico Energy Infrastructure
2005.description: A Category 5 hurricane made landfall near the Texas-Louisiana border shortly after Hurricane Katrina. Impact: Flooded wetlands and severely damaged offshore oil rigs, causing localized crude oil leaks. Casualties: 120 deaths (mostly due to accidents during evacuation)

2005.title: Buncefield Oil Depot Fire and Air Pollution
2005.description: A catastrophic series of explosions at the Hertfordshire fuel storage facility created the largest industrial fire in peacetime Europe. Impact: Triggered a massive toxic black smoke cloud containing soot and aromatic hydrocarbons that covered Southeast England for days. Casualties: 43 injured; caused a regional air quality crisis

2005.title: Texas City Refinery Explosion and Toxic Chemical Leak
2005.description: A catastrophic hydrocarbon explosion at a BP oil refinery released large amounts of toxic gas into the environment. Impact: Dispersed large amounts of toxic volatile organic compounds into the atmosphere surrounding urban residential areas. Casualties: 15 workers killed; over 180 severely injured

2005.title: Severe Flooding in Central European Countries
2005.description: Prolonged heavy rain from a slow-moving low-pressure system caused major flooding in Romania, Switzerland, Austria, and Germany. Impact: Caused severe landslides in Alpine valleys, destroying thousands of hectares of upstream agro-ecological forests. Casualties: Over 60 deaths; estimated economic damage in billions of Euros

2005.title: Buncefield Oil Depot Fire Disaster
2005.description: On December 11, 2005, a major explosion occurred at the Buncefield fuel storage depot in Hemel Hempstead, UK, causing a fire that lasted several days. Impact: Considered one of the largest industrial fires in peacetime Europe. The incident caused severe air pollution and led to reforms in environmental safety at fuel storage facilities. Casualties: 43 injured; no fatalities
2005.source: Health and Safety Executive (HSE), United Kingdom

2005.title: Hurricane Stan Triggers Ecological Landslide Disasters in Central America
2005.description: Despite being only a Category 1 storm, Stan brought massive rainfall to deforested mountain slopes. Impact: Triggered massive mudslides that completely buried several indigenous villages. Casualties: Estimated over 1,500 dead and missing due to mudslides

2005.title: Hurricane Dennis Devastates Caribbean Coastal Vegetation
2005.description: A Category 4 hurricane made a direct hit on Cuba and the Florida Panhandle with extreme storm surges. Impact: Ravaged natural dune strips and severely eroded wetlands protecting migratory birds in the Gulf. Casualties: 89 deaths; 2.5 billion USD in economic losses

2005.title: COP11 Climate Summit in Montreal
2005.description: A major international conference marking the first meeting of the parties to the Kyoto Protocol (CMP1). Impact: Adopted the 'Montreal Roadmap' to extend mandatory emission reduction obligations after the old treaty's expiration. Casualties: None

2005.title: Singapore Reviews and Expands Green Plan 2012
2005.description: The Singapore government conducted a comprehensive review of the Singapore Green Plan 2012 to strengthen environmental and sustainability goals. Impact: Promoted resource management, air quality, clean water, and nature conservation in one of the world's most urbanized nations. Casualties: None

2010.title: Deepwater Horizon Oil Spill
2010.description: An explosion on a BP drilling rig in the Gulf of Mexico leaked approximately 4.9 million barrels of crude oil into the ocean over 87 days. Impact: Evaluated as one of the largest marine environmental disasters in US history. It caused widespread ecological damage to seabirds, turtles, dolphins, and deep-sea ecosystems. Casualties: 11 workers killed; immeasurable ecological damage

2010.title: Earthquake Devastates Haiti
2010.description: A 7.0 magnitude earthquake struck near the capital Port-au-Prince, flattening infrastructure and the healthcare system. Impact: Flattened urban infrastructure and collapsed sanitation systems, indirectly causing a rapid cholera outbreak due to clean water shortages. Casualties: Estimated 220,000 - 300,000 deaths

2010.title: Widespread Heatwave and Wildfires in Russia
2010.description: Record-high temperatures caused hundreds of forest and peat fires around Moscow. Impact: Toxic smog covered Moscow, burning hundreds of thousands of hectares of forest and causing widespread crop damage. Casualties: Estimated 56,000 deaths related to record heat and toxic smog.

2010.title: Catastrophic Floods in Pakistan
2010.description: Unprecedented extreme monsoon rains flooded about one-fifth of Pakistan's total land area. Impact: Washed away millions of hectares of fertile farmland, destroyed riverine ecosystems, and caused localized famine. Casualties: Over 2,000 deaths; 20 million left homeless

2010.title: Eyjafjallajökull Volcano Eruption
2010.description: An ice-capped volcano in Iceland erupted violently, sending massive amounts of ash thousands of meters into the air. Impact: Froze European airspace for days; ash contaminated nearby glacial rivers. Casualties: No deaths; historic aviation disruption

2010.title: Ajka Red Mud Disaster
2010.description: A red mud reservoir dam at an aluminum plant failed, releasing about 1 million m³ of highly alkaline toxic waste. Impact: Severely polluted the Marcal River and surrounding areas, causing massive damage to local ecosystems and farmland. Casualties: 10 deaths; hundreds suffered chemical burns

2010.title: Chile Earthquake and Tsunami
2010.description: An 8.8 magnitude mega-earthquake off the Maule region triggered a tsunami that swept the coast. Impact: The tsunami ravaged coastal ecological reserves and changed the geological structure of South America's coastline. Casualties: 525 deaths

2010.title: COP16 Climate Summit in Cancún
2010.description: An international conference established the Green Climate Fund to support developing nations. Impact: Reached the Cancún Agreements, bringing voluntary emission reduction pledges into a formal UN framework. Casualties: None

2010.title: Record Drought in the Amazon Basin
2010.description: A drought more severe than the 2005 event lowered water levels in Amazon tributaries to unprecedented levels. Impact: Reduced the Amazon's carbon absorption capacity, increased fire risk, and caused significant losses to regional ecosystems. Casualties: Massive loss of plant biodiversity

2010.title: Yushu Earthquake
2010.description: A 6.9 magnitude earthquake hit the ecologically sensitive high-altitude region of the Tibetan Plateau. Impact: Triggered severe landslides that disrupted headwaters of major Asian rivers. Casualties: Over 2,600 deaths

2010.title: Catastrophic Merapi Eruption
2010.description: Indonesia's most active volcano erupted pyroclastic flows (hot ash and gas) down its slopes. Impact: Burned thousands of hectares of slope agricultural vegetation; forced 350,000 to evacuate. Casualties: 353 deaths

2010.title: Cyclone Xynthia Sweeps Europe
2010.description: A winter storm with hurricane-force winds and storm surges breached sea dikes in France and Spain. Impact: Widespread salinization damaged coastal farmland and destroyed wetland habitats. Casualties: About 63 deaths

2010.title: Historic Floods in Northeastern Brazil
2010.description: Unusual heavy rains caused many small dams to burst in Alagoas and Pernambuco. Impact: Dozens of towns flattened; mudflows buried thousands of hectares of tropical crops. Casualties: 51 deaths; over 100,000 left homeless

2010.title: Mount Sinabung Awakens
2010.description: Mount Sinabung unexpectedly erupted after 400 years of dormancy, threatening North Sumatra. Impact: Coated vast agricultural areas in thick ash, beginning a decade of geological activity. Casualties: 2 deaths from medical conditions during urgent evacuation

2010.title: Sahel Drought and Food Crisis
2010.description: Severe lack of rain in the Sahara desert fringe led to the depletion of natural water sources. Impact: Desertified large grassland areas, killing livestock and threatening the food security of 10 million people. Casualties: Thousands died indirectly from malnutrition and famine

2015.title: Signing of the Paris Agreement (COP21)
2015.description: A historic global treaty adopted by 196 parties to limit global temperature rise below 1.5°C. Impact: Marked the largest international legal turning point for the environment, unifying global energy transition actions. Casualties: None

2015.title: Gorkha Earthquake Devastates Nepal
2015.description: A 7.8 magnitude earthquake flattened much of Kathmandu and triggered an avalanche on Mt Everest. Impact: Deformed Himalayan slopes and destroyed conservation geological structures and protective forests. Casualties: Nearly 9,000 deaths; 22,000 injured

2015.title: Mariana Dam Disaster
2015.description: The Fundão iron ore tailings dam owned by Samarco failed, releasing 50 million m³ of toxic mud into the Doce River. Impact: Regarded as one of Brazil's worst environmental disasters, causing widespread pollution of the Doce River basin and long-term impacts on aquatic ecosystems. Casualties: 19 deaths

2015.title: Southeast Asian Haze Crisis
2015.description: Widespread peatland forest fires in Sumatra and Kalimantan went out of control due to El Niño. Impact: Air Quality Index (AQI) exceeded 2000; daily greenhouse gas emissions surpassed those of the entire US economy. Casualties: Studies estimate tens of thousands to about 100,000 premature deaths related to air pollution

2015.title: Third Global Coral Bleaching Event
2015.description: Extreme ocean heatwaves due to a record El Niño weakened and killed coral globally. Impact: Lost 30% of the Great Barrier Reef and thousands of km² of coral in the Pacific and Indian Oceans. Casualties: Irreversible short-term damage to the marine biosphere

2015.title: Gold King Mine Waste Water Spill
2015.description: EPA contractors accidentally breached a dam at an old gold mine, releasing 11 million liters of heavy metal-contaminated water downstream. Impact: Turned the Animas River mustard yellow, poisoning glacial river ecosystems with lead, arsenic, and cadmium. Casualties: No direct human deaths

2015.title: Tianjin Chemical Explosions
2015.description: Series of explosions at an illegal chemical warehouse storing ammonium nitrate and sodium cyanide with earthquake-like force. Impact: Created a chemical dust cloud around the port area; heavily poisoned nearby water sources. Casualties: 173 deaths; hundreds injured

2015.title: Historic South Indian Floods (Chennai)
2015.description: Northeast monsoon rainfall reached a 100-year record, submerging Chennai and southern India. Impact: Destroyed natural wetland systems due to poor urban planning; caused widespread clean water pollution. Casualties: Over 500 deaths

2015.title: Peak of the Multi-Year California Drought
2015.description: The fourth consecutive year of a century-scale drought forced state authorities to mandate 25% water cuts for the first time. Impact: Millions of trees in the Sierra Nevada died (fueling future wildfires); land subsidence occurred due to groundwater extraction. Casualties: Agricultural losses reached billions of USD

2015.title: Hurricane Patricia
2015.description: The strongest tropical cyclone ever recorded in the Western Hemisphere, with sustained winds up to 345 km/h. Impact: Though it weakened quickly at landfall, it devastated mangroves and coastal hills in Jalisco. Casualties: 6 deaths

2015.title: Unexpected Calbuco Volcano Eruption
2015.description: After 43 years of dormancy, this volcano in southern Chile suddenly sent ash plumes 20km into the stratosphere. Impact: Ash choked surrounding ecological vegetation; affected aquaculture water sources (particularly salmon). Casualties: No direct human fatalities

2015.title: Cyclone Pam Devastates the South Pacific
2015.description: A Category 5 storm with destructive winds swept directly through the Vanuatu archipelago. Impact: Worst natural disaster in Vanuatu's history, destroying 96% of the island's food crops and vegetation. Casualties: 16 deaths

2015.title: Historic Winter Floods in the UK
2015.description: Storm Desmond brought a record 24-hour rainfall (341.4 mm), devastating Cumbria and Lancashire. Impact: Floodwaters isolated historic towns, exceeding the capacity of Britain's river basin ecological defenses. Casualties: About 3 deaths; insurance losses reached 1.5 billion GBP

2015.title: Texas-Oklahoma Flash Floods
2015.description: Slow-moving storm systems dumped massive rainfall in May, abruptly ending a drought but causing catastrophic flash flooding. Impact: The Blanco River rose to record levels, uprooting ancient cypress trees and eroding natural riverbank structures. Casualties: At least 28 deaths

2015.title: Illapel Earthquake
2015.description: An 8.3 magnitude earthquake shook the Coquimbo region, triggering a tsunami along the Pacific coast. Impact: Large waves destroyed coastal mangrove wetlands and devastated nearby small fishing villages. Casualties: 15 deaths

2020.title: Australia's 'Black Summer' Bushfires
2020.description: The peak phase of a prolonged bushfire disaster that blanketed the East Coast of Australia in fire due to extreme drought. Impact: Burned 18 million hectares of forest; killed or displaced more than 3 billion wild animals. Casualties: 34 direct deaths

2020.title: Western US Wildfires
2020.description: Extreme heat and dry thunderstorms triggered thousands of fires, turning California's skies an apocalyptic orange. Impact: Over 1.6 million hectares of forest in California burned; air quality dropped to hazardous levels across the West Coast. Casualties: Over 30 deaths

2020.title: Super Cyclone Amphan
2020.description: The strongest cyclone in the Bay of Bengal in over two centuries made landfall on the India-Bangladesh border. Impact: Destroyed the Sundarbans, the world's largest mangrove ecosystem, and caused saltwater intrusion that crippled local agriculture. Casualties: 128 deaths; 13 billion USD in damages

2020.title: East African Desert Locust Plague
2020.description: An explosion of hundreds of billions of locusts due to warm weather and unusual rains in the Arabian Peninsula that spread to East Africa. Impact: Wiped out hundreds of thousands of hectares of food crops, threatening the ecological livelihoods of over 25 million people. Casualties: Widespread food security crisis

2020.title: Norilsk Oil Spill Disaster
2020.description: Melting permafrost caused a fuel tank at a Siberian power plant to collapse, spilling diesel into the Arctic. Impact: Over 21,000 tons of oil dyed the Ambarnaya River red, creating the worst Arctic ecological disaster in Russia's history. Casualties: Arctic wetland ecosystems heavily damaged

2020.title: Super Typhoon Goni
2020.description: The world's strongest landfalling cyclone in 2020, with winds exceeding 315 km/h, devastated the Bicol region of the Philippines. Impact: Heavy rain triggered massive lahars (mudflows) from Mayon Volcano, burying thousands of hectares of farmland. Casualties: 32 deaths

2020.title: MV Wakashio Oil Spill
2020.description: A Japanese bulk carrier ran aground on the pristine Pointe d'Esny reef, causing an oil spill. Impact: 1,000 tons of leaked oil destroyed mangrove ecological reserves and fragile Indian Ocean coral reefs. Casualties: No direct human fatalities

2020.title: Record Atlantic Hurricane Season
2020.description: Warming sea temperatures caused a record 30 named storms in the Atlantic in one season. Impact: Successive major storms caused persistent coastal erosion and exhausted wetland vegetation in Louisiana. Casualties: Over 400 deaths across the region

2020.title: Kamchatka Ecological Disaster
2020.description: An unusual toxic algae bloom combined with suspected military chemical pollution killed massive amounts of seabed organisms. Impact: About 95% of seabed organisms (sea urchins, starfish, seals) along the Avacha Bay coast were killed. Casualties: Several surfers suffered corneal burns

2020.title: Pantanal Wetland Wildfires
2020.description: The world's largest tropical wetland suffered its worst drought in 50 years, leading to uncontrollable fires. Impact: Over 30% of the wetlands (4 million hectares) were turned to ash, killing thousands of jaguars and caimans. Casualties: Unprecedented loss of biodiversity

2020.title: Historic Central Vietnam Floods
2020.description: A series of consecutive storms and depressions dumped massive rainfall on the coastal central region of Vietnam. Impact: Triggered catastrophic landslides (Rao Trang 3, Tra Leng) and destroyed all crops and plantations. Casualties: Over 200 dead and missing

2020.title: Taal Volcano Eruption
2020.description: A volcano located within a lake south of Manila erupted with a massive ash plume and volcanic lightning. Impact: A layer of volcanic ash buried the entire agricultural ecosystem around the lake and destroyed fisheries. Casualties: 39 deaths due to medical complications and accidents during evacuation

2020.title: Sudan's Worst Floods in Decades
2020.description: The Nile River rose to its highest level in 100 years due to extreme rainfall in the basin. Impact: Submerged millions of hectares of riverside farmland, threatened historic pyramids, and collapsed food sources. Casualties: At least 150 deaths; hundreds of thousands homeless

2020.title: US Midwest Derecho
2020.description: A widespread inland windstorm (derecho) swept across the Midwest with Category 3-equivalent winds. Impact: Flattened over 14 million acres of corn and soybeans; broke 65% of the long-term tree canopy in Cedar Rapids. Casualties: 4 deaths; 11 billion USD in economic damage

2020.title: Peak Assam Floods
2020.description: Combination of cyclonic storms and monsoon activity overflowed the Brahmaputra River. Impact: Flooded 85% of Kaziranga National Park, drowning hundreds of rare one-horned rhinoceroses. Casualties: Over 120 direct deaths

2025.title: COP30 Climate Summit in Belém
2025.description: The largest climate diplomacy event of the decade, aimed at reviewing the Paris Agreement, held at the gateway to the Amazon. Impact: Expected to reshape Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs) to keep temperature rise below 1.5°C. Casualties: None

2025.title: Antarctic Summer Sea Ice Hits New Low
2025.description: The area of reflective sea ice in Antarctica shrunk to consecutive record lows due to warming ocean currents. Impact: Exacerbates the rate of global sea-level rise and directly threatens Emperor penguin colonies. Casualties: Biological threat to polar ecosystems
2025.source: National Snow and Ice Data Center (NSIDC)

2025.title: Global Plastic Treaty Enters into Force
2025.description: The first legally binding international treaty to control plastic and microplastic pollution globally. Impact: Lays the legal foundation for ending marine plastic waste and banning microplastics in many nations. Casualties: None

2025.title: New Record Drought in the Amazon
2025.description: Warming in the North Atlantic sucked moisture from tropical South America, causing giant rivers to turn into deserts again. Impact: Stalled hydroelectricity, isolated indigenous peoples, and turned parts of the rainforest into net CO2 emitters. Casualties: Severe ecological crisis

2025.title: Massive Atmospheric River Strikes the US West Coast
2025.description: Giant bands of water vapor from the ocean repeatedly slammed into California, causing record cumulative rainfall. Impact: Rapidly replenished dry lakes but breached numerous small dams and eroded coastal cliffs. Casualties: Tens of billions of USD in infrastructure damage

2025.title: Mediterranean Marine Heatwave Crisis
2025.description: Mediterranean Sea surface temperatures remained above the 30°C threshold for many summer weeks. Impact: Caused widespread bleaching of temperate corals and triggered an explosion of invasive species from the Red Sea. Casualties: Large-scale losses for the European fishing industry

2025.title: Mass Bleaching of the Great Barrier Reef (New Wave)
2025.description: Prolonged tropical heat caused the next wave of bleaching to spread to deeper areas never before affected. Impact: Sparked global debate on placing this Natural Heritage site on the 'In Danger' list. Casualties: Risk of total loss of the world's largest coral reef
2025.source: Great Barrier Reef Marine Park Authority

2025.title: Unusual Super Cyclone in the Bay of Bengal
2025.description: A cyclone fueled by abnormally warm sea temperatures made landfall with great intensity, ravaging coastal ecosystems. Impact: Caused further salinization of much of the Ganges Delta farmland and accelerated coastal erosion. Casualties: Livelihood threat for millions of people

2025.title: Historic Summer Flooding in Central Europe
2025.description: Stationary low-pressure systems dumped continuous rain for days in the Rhine and Danube basins. Impact: Submerged riverine ecological corridors and caused overflows at old industrial chemical plants. Casualties: Massive infrastructure damage

2025.title: Record Dust Storm Covers East Asia
2025.description: Desertification combined with an extreme winter created the largest Gobi desert dust plume in modern history striking Beijing. Impact: Fine particulate matter (PM10) exceeded 2000, hindering photosynthesis in North China Plain agriculture and harming health. Casualties: Explosion of respiratory emergencies in major cities

2025.title: Himalayan Glacial Lake Outburst Flood (GLOF)
2025.description: Rapid glacial melt caused a large glacial lake at 5,000m altitude to breach its natural dam. Impact: Created a flash flood that swept away indigenous villages, hydroelectric facilities, and tore through valley slopes. Casualties: Many missing; permanently altered regional terrain

2025.title: Peak Tropical Haze/Wildfire Season
2025.description: A prolonged dry season caused slash-and-burn activities in Southeast Asian peatlands to spiral out of control. Impact: Transboundary haze blanketed the region, threatening the last habitat of wild Borneo orangutans. Casualties: Severely impacted quality of life for regional residents

2025.title: South Asia Heatwave Disaster
2025.description: A trapped heat dome pushed perceived temperatures beyond human physiological limits (>50°C) for several days. Impact: Killed massive amounts of urban birds, caused widespread power outages, and severely depleted surface water networks. Casualties: Thousands died from heatstroke among outdoor laborers

2025.title: Drought Threat in the Horn of Africa Continues
2025.description: Consecutive rain failures caused the East African savanna ecosystem to fall into a state of severe soil nutrient collapse. Impact: Widespread hunger forced wildlife out of reserves to compete for water with livestock. Casualties: Major humanitarian and conservation crisis

2025.title: Accelerated Ice Melt in Greenland
2025.description: Arctic summer temperatures reached unusually high levels, triggering the largest glacial melt outflow into the ocean in history. Impact: Altered the salinity of the North Atlantic, risking a slowdown of the AMOC ocean current. Casualties: Long-term consequences for European climate
